scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PCs in the IT Department (192.168.1.x) report they cannot reach
their gateway (192.168.1.1) or anything off-subnet. CS Dept PCs
(192.168.2.x) and all other zones are unaffected. Identify the
failure.

injection.action: bring down the bridge that carries IT Dept LAN

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show br0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch0 br0 (L2 fabric for IT Dept LAN)
Mechanism: switch0's br0 carries the IT Dept LAN's path to
  router0's 192.168.1.1 SVI. With br0 down, IT hosts lose their
  gateway and all off-subnet reachability. Other subnets are on
  different switches/bridges, so they're unaffected.
Localization: switch0
Root cause: br0 administratively down on switch0
Fix: `ip link set br0 up` on switch0
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br0 up` on switch0

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: Layer-2 bridging on the IT access switch (switch0). The Linux bridge interface br0 that should forward between router0.eth0 (link_r0_sw0) and the IT LAN (lan_it) is down.

Mechanism: IT hosts and their default gateway cannot resolve each other’s MAC addresses, so ARP fails. That produces “Destination Host Unreachable” locally on both ends when pinging, and prevents any off-subnet traffic (which depends on reaching the gateway). Other subnets use different switches and are unaffected.

Localization: 
- it_lab1 -> 192.168.1.1: Destination Host Unreachable from 192.168.1.3 (it_lab1), confirming no L2 path.
- router0 -> 192.168.1.3: Destination Host Unreachable from 192.168.1.1 (router0), confirming the break is between router0.eth0 and IT hosts.
- On switch0, eth0 and eth1 are enslaved to br0 (“master br0”), but br0 is DOWN: “2: br0 … state DOWN”. With the bridge down, no frames are forwarded between ports despite both links showing “Link detected: yes.”

Root cause: The bridge br0 on switch0 is administratively down, disabling L2 forwarding for the 192.168.1.0/24 segment.

Corrective fix: Bring the bridge up and ensure it remains enabled at boot: on switch0, ip link set br0 up (or start the bridge service if managed by systemd/networkd). Verify ports remain enslaved to br0 and forwarding (bridge link/show), and confirm IT hosts can ARP/ping 192.168.1.1 afterward.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly identifies the affected device as switch0 (the IT access switch) in the diagnosis.
The report explicitly names the Linux bridge br0 on switch0 as the failed L2 fabric (br0 DOWN), satisfying the component identification requirement.
The agent explicitly localizes the fault to the IT access switch/bridge and states other subnets on different switches are unaffected, matching the required scope distinction.
Correctly recommends bringing br0 up with 'ip link set br0 up' and ensuring it remains enabled at boot, matching the expected fix.

The investigator observed br0 on switch0 without the UP flag and reciprocal “Destination Host Unreachable” ping failures between an IT host and router; these observations support the conclusion that the bridge being administratively down is preventing L2 forwarding. A minor unsupported detail (explicit 'Link detected: yes' / slave listing) appears in the writeup but does not undermine the main diagnosis.
